claims.says: Descend the Southwest Couloir (standard route) toward the approach side.

Finish down North Fork Bridge Creek and the PCT back to Highway 20. / Return to the Bridge Creek trailhead.

Because the standard descent drops into the Park Creek/Stehekin drainage - the opposite side of the mountain from the Bridge Creek approach used to reach Megalodon Ridge - getting back to a car at Rainy Pass is a long second act: parties either arrange a shuttle or hike out via Park Creek Trail and Thunder Creek Trail to the North Cascades Highway at Colonial Creek...

contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft (7500) and loss_ft (8700) are themselves asymmetric by 1,200 ft, i.e. the route's own numbers imply ending lower than the start rather than a symmetric out-and-back — consistent with descent_text's Park Creek/Stehekin ending, not with the itinerary's claim of returning to the same trailhead. descent_text + rappel_detail (detailed, technical) agree; itinerary/timing/short descent field appear to have wrongly assumed a simple reversal.

contradictions.fact: Whether the North Ridge is reached via Lucky Pass

claims.says: Via McAllister Camp (~6 mi in), then the ridge below Tricouni Peak to the Borealis Glacier and Lucky Pass (7,200 ft) col, finishing up Primus's ridge.
...the North Ridge is reached by traversing around the lake instead of climbing the glacier from camp.
...reached by descending a couloir onto an unnamed glacier north of Primus (accessed from the North Klawatti Glacier after climbing Austera Peak the same day)...

LUCKY PASS IS NOT THIS ROUTE. If you are standing at a col at about 7,200 ft at the head of the Borealis Glacier, with Tricouni Peak's route splitting off east, you are at the start of the East Slope — a class 3 walk. The North Ridge is reached by turning away from that pass, not through it.

contradictions.why: The waypoints summit note routes the ascent through the Borealis Glacier and Lucky Pass col, directly contradicting this route's own approach/overview/beta/approach_variants, which say the North Ridge is reached by going AROUND the lake or via a glacier/couloir north of the peak — and approach_variants explicitly warns that reaching Lucky Pass means you are actually on the East Slope, not the North Ridge.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, overview, beta and approach_variants.baseFinding (4 fields, including an explicit warning) agree the ascent avoids Lucky Pass; the waypoints note is the outlier and would send a climber up the wrong route.
